title: Fair terms and a clinging expectation

captions.emotions: Clinging to needed confirmation of attention

meaning: You can find fair terms for a promise while noticing how a strong expectation of attention can remain even after a clear reply.
text: Precise agreement does not always settle a strong expectation immediately. The Chariot in the physical position of Vishuddha clarifies a request into concrete terms. Justice in energy supports an honest proportion within a mutual promise. The Devil in emotions clings to necessary confirmation of attention: an answer is wanted alongside a particular feeling from it. A request can gain a real subject without making its emotional weight another person’s obligation to respond in one way immediately. Consent and reassurance can arrive at different times.

For example, you discuss putting phones aside during shared conversation. Questions clarify which exchanges need full attention and how to mention an urgent reply. **A fair condition need not settle every feeling immediately.** Concrete participation can be agreed while a brief pause still disappoints. That feeling can receive words separately instead of proving consent insincere or requiring permanent uninterrupted attention to restore closeness.

The difficulty is refining terms until the single reaction that settles attachment appears. The rule grows stricter while actual conversation shrinks. Naming a need for reassurance directly restores honesty. Support can be chosen separately from a permanent commitment, leaving small pauses free from becoming repeated demonstrations of who matters to whom or how much attention someone deserves.
